edge_handoffs.note: The test imports component 101's real resolveTransferAnswer, executes it, and passes the produced object into component 102's real TransferAssessmentService.toPublicAssessment, so the consumer receives the actual upstream artifact rather than a hand-authored fixture.

The test loads component 104's real adapter and one frozen case from its committed cases.json, then calls buildTransferTargetRequest, which calls loadSharedRequestContract() and therefore requires the actual tutor-system/src/services/ecologicalTutorCall.ts and invokes the real buildTransferTutorRequestContextV3 and buildTransferTutorRequestV3. The assertions consume that produced request: its contract identity must equal the identity the frozen manifest pins, reordered and duplicated input must yield a byte-identical user message, no evaluator-only key may appear, and a manifest whose budget or thinking flag diverges from the production source must be refused. Nothing on either side is hand-authored.

The test constructs component 102's real TransferAssessmentService with an injected transport so it returns the actual prepare_turn envelope, then passes that same object into component 103's real transferAssessmentUiAdapter: createReviewCandidate for the reviewed-send scope, publicAssessmentForDecision for the learner projection, and classifyAssessmentFailure for the three scoped server codes. Component 103's own gate suite is also run in integration at 16 suites / 100 tests. The production half of the same file separately asserts the prepare_turn wrapper, the null item id, the no-write rule, and the three failure codes against the Edge Function source.
